data.title: Story map — kadence
body: # Story map — kadence
- **Date:** 2026-09-16. Replaces the 2026-09-08 map, which was written at `0.2.1` in Ukrainian and followed one person through a sprint.
- **Method:** Jeff Patton, *User Story Mapping* (2014), via the `product-story-mapping` skill: backbone of user activities, steps under each, stories under each step, release slices drawn across.
- **Product state:** `kadence@0.4.1` published 2026-09-13. Some work is only in the working tree (the "Unreleased" section of `CHANGELOG.md`).

- **Feature truth:** the 2026-09-16 product inventory, which was read from the binary, `schema --json`, `CHANGELOG.md` and `src/`. Where an older product document disagrees with it, the inventory wins.
- **Strategy truth:** [strategy.md](DOC-35) (ICP, gates, dates) and [roadmap-to-1.0.md](DOC-32) (G1–G7).

- **Evidence status:** as of today there are 0 interviews, 0 pilots and 0 external users ([strategy §0](DOC-35)). Every story below comes from the code or from a decision. None comes from watching a team we don't control. The slices are bets, and their gates are the tests.
## Who, and what they are trying to do

**Segment.** A product company or agency with **3–8 developers** on shared repositories. At least 2 of them use Claude Code, Cursor or Codex daily. Sharpened by the discovery verdict to *repositories where more than one human, or more than one agent vendor, works* ([strategy §1](DOC-35)).
**Personas.** The map follows two people, because the North Star needs both:
| | Who | Role in the first 14 days |

| **P1 — the tech lead** | Staff, senior or founding engineer. Writes `CLAUDE.md` and can add `.kadence/` alone. | Adopts it, sets it up, records the first decisions, and brings the second person in. |

| **P2 — the second author** | A teammate, plus the agent sessions that teammate runs. May never have heard of kadence. | Picks up work someone else started and writes to the journal without being asked. |
| *Agent* | Any coding agent session, from any vendor | Acts inside activities 2–5. It is not a separate journey here. See "What this map still cannot show". |
**Narrative (the job, from [strategy §1](DOC-35)).**
> When I start an agent session on work someone else started, I want the agent to already know what was tried, decided and blocked, so I don't re-explain and it doesn't repeat a rejected path.

**What activation means.** The North Star is *a repository whose `.kadence/events` holds entries from ≥ 2 authors 14 days after `init`*. The activation slice below is sized to that sentence and nothing more.
## Backbone
1. Adopt  →  2. Capture work  →  3. Hand off  →  4. Decide & record why  →  5. Review progress  →  6. Leave
(P1)        (P1, P2, agent)     (P2, agent)      (P1, P2, agent)            (P1, manager)          (P1)

Each activity is something a person does, not a feature we built. "Leave" is on the backbone on purpose. A tech lead who cannot see the exit won't take the entrance, and the pilot offer already promises "to leave: `rm -rf .kadence` and discard those edits" ([probe-b-outreach.md](../research/probe-b-outreach.md)).
**Status legend**
- **Shipped (0.x.y)**: in a published npm version, with the first version that carried it
- **Unreleased**: in the working tree and `CHANGELOG.md` [Unreleased], but not on npm
- **Gap**: not built, not documented, or never observed working. **Gap ★** marks a gap on the activation path.
## 1. Adopt
| Step | Story | Status |

| **1.1 Decide to try** | As P1, I can read in one place what kadence writes, what it never does, and what is not proven, before I install anything | Shipped: README "Honest status" and "What it costs you". **Gap:** the site copy was written for 0.2 and is stale until [landing-copy.md](DOC-25) ships |
| | As P1, I can see how to remove it again before I add it | **Gap ★**: the steps are only in the pilot message, not in the README or on the site |
| **1.2 Install** | As P1, I install with `npm install -g kadence` on Node ≥ 20 | Shipped (0.1.0) |
| | As P1 on Windows, or on pnpm, yarn or bun, I can trust the install works | **Gap**: CI runs Linux on Node 20 and 22 only, with no install matrix (G4) |

| **1.3 Initialise** | As P1, `kadence init` creates `.kadence/`, writes a marked section into both `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`, and adds `.kadence/state.json` to `.gitignore`, without touching text a human wrote | Shipped (0.1.0; `CLAUDE.md` since 0.2.1; version marker since 0.3.0) |
| | As P1 on Claude Code, `init --hooks` makes every new session start with `kadence prime` | Shipped (0.4.0) |
| | As P1, I am told plainly that nothing was committed and that committing is my call | Shipped (0.1.0, the `init` message) |

| **1.4 Fit it to the team** | As P1, I set the columns (`board config --statuses`), the column cycle time counts from (`--started`), and a Definition of Done (`--dod`) | Shipped (statuses 0.1.0; `--started` and `--dod` 0.4.1) |
| | As P1, I can take back a criterion that should not be on a task | **Gap**: there is no `task ac remove`, and the default DoD wording is engineering-shaped |
| **1.5 Bring existing work in** | As P1 on Backlog.md or Beads, I can import what is already there | **Gap**: the importer is planned for 0.6, and only if the Oct 19 gate opens P4 |
| | As P1, I can link the ADRs we already have to decisions | Shipped (0.3.0, `decision add --doc`). There is no bulk import, which is fine for a pilot |
| **1.6 Check it works** | As P1, I can ask kadence whether this repository's journal is healthy | **Gap**: no `doctor` (G5, Later) |
| | As a stranger with only the README, I reach `task add` and an agent running `prime` in ≤ 10 minutes | **Gap ★ (never observed)**: this is self-serve test KR 3.4, not yet run |
## 2. Capture work
| Step | Story | Status |
| **2.1 Write it down** | As P1 or P2, I add a task with type, priority, estimate, due date, labels and parent (`task add`) | Shipped (0.1.0) |
| | As P2's agent, I add or edit tasks, and my events say `source: agent` | Shipped (events 0.1.x; comments and history 0.4.1) |
| | As P1, I start from a template (`--template bug`) | Shipped (0.1.0) |
| **2.2 Say what done means** | As P1, I add acceptance criteria that P2 or an agent can check off (`task ac add\|check`) | Shipped (0.4.1) |
| | As P1, every new task starts with the team's DoD, copied rather than referenced | Shipped (0.4.1) |
| **2.3 Shape the work** | As P1, I group work under an outcome (`milestone create\|add`) | Shipped (0.4.1) |
| | As P1, I say what blocks what (`task block`). Cycles are reported, not rejected | Shipped (0.1.0) |
| | As P1, I link the design doc, creating it from a template when it is missing (`task doc add`) | Shipped (link 0.3.0; create-and-link 0.4.1) |

| **2.4 Mark how carefully to work** | As P1, I mark impact with labels (`impact-critical`), and an agent asking what it can start sees them | Shipped mechanism: labels 0.1.0, deltas 0.4.1, `labels` in `ready --json` 0.4.1. **Gap:** the recipe is undocumented, including how impact differs from `priority` ([tech-lead feedback, Finding 4](../research/tech-lead-feedback-2026-09-10.md)) |
## 3. Hand off to a teammate or an agent
This is the activity the job statement is about, and the one the North Star counts.
| Step | Story | Status |

| **3.1 Learn the tool is here** | As P2, when P1 adds kadence, I find out it exists, what it is for, and the one command to try | **Gap ★**: nothing in the product does this. The only path is a hand-written "teammate nudge" that P1 has to send ([probe-b-outreach.md](../research/probe-b-outreach.md)). The `init` message names no next step for anyone else |

| | As P2, I install kadence, or my session hook fails in a way I understand | **Gap ★ (unverified)**: nobody has checked what a `SessionStart` hook running `kadence prime` does on a machine without kadence |

| **3.2 Start a session with context** | As P2's agent on Claude Code, my session opens with the sprint, my work, what is ready, the decisions in force and the latest notes (`prime`, ≤ 40 lines and ≤ 3 KB by test) | Shipped (0.4.0) |

| | As P2's agent on Cursor or Codex, I am pointed at `prime` by `AGENTS.md` | Shipped (0.1.0 / 0.2.1). **Gap ★:** those agents have no hook, so running `prime` depends on the agent following the instruction, and that has never been observed |
| **3.3 Find what to pick up** | As P2 or an agent, `ready` shows what is open, unblocked, unclaimed and not yet started, and says why when it is empty | Shipped (0.4.0; fixed in 0.4.1) |
| | As P2, I see only the tasks this branch is about (`task list --branch`) | Shipped (0.4.1) |

| **3.4 Take it** | As P2 or an agent, `task claim` takes the top of `ready` in one step. If two machines claim the same task, it reads `contested` with both names rather than silently picking one | Shipped (0.4.0; ADR-011) |

| **3.5 Read what happened** | As P2's agent, one call (`task show --json`) returns status, blockers, criteria, comments, decisions, notes and full history | Shipped (0.1.0; decisions 0.3.0; notes and claim 0.4.0) |
| **3.6 Leave a trail** | As P2 or an agent, I comment, add a note to the task (`note --task`), check criteria and log a correction to time spent | Shipped (0.1.0; `note` 0.4.0) |
| | As P2, the claim ends when the task reaches `done`, so nobody has to remember to release it | Shipped (0.4.0) |
| **3.7 Know who did what** | As P1, I can tell a person's own events from their agent's, even though both share one git identity (`KADENCE_SOURCE=agent`) | Shipped (0.4.1 on comments and history) |
| | As P1, I can tell which model did the work | **Gap, deliberately**: not now ([tech-lead feedback, Finding 3](../research/tech-lead-feedback-2026-09-10.md)) |
| | As P2 with two machines and two `user.email` values, I am still one author | **Gap**: open question 2 in SPEC §9 |
| **3.8 Merge branches** | As P2, my branch and P1's branch both touched the same task, and the merge has no conflict and says so | Shipped (0.1.0; `test/integration/merge.test.ts`) |
## 4. Decide and record why
| Step | Story | Status |

| **4.1 Record a decision** | As P1, I record a decision with a required `--why` and the alternatives that lost (`--rejected`), linked to a task | Shipped (0.3.0). **Unreleased fix, Gap ★:** passing `--rejected` twice crashes `decision add` in 0.4.1. That is the most natural way to record two rejected options, and the fix is not on npm yet |
| **4.2 Change your mind** | As P1, I supersede a decision in one event, and the backward link is derived | Shipped (0.3.0; ADR-010) |
| **4.3 Record what you learned** | As P2 or an agent, I record something learned that was never a choice (`note`) | Shipped (0.4.0) |

| **4.4 Have the next session read it** | As P2's agent, the decision P1 recorded yesterday appears in my `prime` and in `task show --json` | Shipped (0.3.0 / 0.4.0). **Gap ★ (never observed):** no agent outside this repository has been seen reading a decision and acting on it. Pilot 0 on Sep 25 is the first chance ([strategy KR 3.1](DOC-35)) |
| **4.5 Show decisions to people outside the repo** | As P1, decisions in force appear in the HTML board export | Shipped (0.4.1) |
## 5. Review progress
Reports are here because the journal happens to know the answers. They are not the reason anyone adopts ([strategy §1](DOC-35)). None of them is on the activation path.
| Step | Story | Status |

| **5.1 Look at the board** | As P1, I see the board in the terminal (`board`) or work it with keys and mouse (`ui`: `R` ready, `C` claim, `b` branch, `M` milestone) | Shipped (0.1.0; keys 0.4.1). TUI checked by hand only |

| **5.2 See what nobody is looking at** | As P1, I get the stalled, unowned, stale-claim and dead-blocker lists (`report attention`), and a line in `prime` when there is something to say | Shipped (0.4.1). It only knows what was written to it |

| | As P1, I see that someone other than me has started writing to the journal | **Gap ★**: `stats` counts by assignee, not by author. The day-14 question has to be answered with `git log --format=%ae -- .kadence` |
| **5.3 Summarise for the team** | As P1, I see counts, blockers, contested claims and recent velocity (`stats`) | Shipped (0.4.1) |
| | As P1, I close a sprint and get points, hours and carry-over (`sprint close`, `sprint burndown`) | Shipped (0.1.0) |
| **5.4 Answer "how long do things take"** | As P1, `report flow` and `report cfd` give percentiles, WIP, aging work and tasks per column per day | Shipped (0.4.1) |
| | As P1, `report velocity` gives a low/median/high range, `report workload` shows who carries what, and `report --list` names all the reports | Unreleased |
| **5.5 Share outside the repo** | As P1, I send a manager one self-contained HTML or Markdown board (`board export`) | Shipped (0.4.1) |
| | As P1, I send one report as a page with charts (`report <name> --html`) | Unreleased |
| | As P1, I publish chosen tasks to GitHub Issues one way (`@kadence/github`) | Shipped (separate package 0.1.0, experiment) |
| | As P1, I get burnup, time in status or epic rollup | Gap (Later, reports discovery) |
## 6. Leave or uninstall
| Step | Story | Status |
| **6.1 Stop** | As P1, stopping costs nothing: no daemon, server or account is left behind | Shipped (by design) |
| **6.2 Keep a record** | As P1, before removing it, I export a snapshot a human can read (`board export --md\|--html`) | Shipped (0.4.1) |
| | As P1, the events stay readable as plain JSON without kadence | Shipped (0.1.0; ADR-002) |

| **6.3 Remove** | As P1, one documented procedure removes everything `init` added: `.kadence/`, the section between `<!-- kadence:begin -->` and `<!-- kadence:end -->` in `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` (or the file, if `init` created it), the `.gitignore` line, and the `kadence prime` hook if `--hooks` was used | **Gap ★**: there is no command and no written procedure outside the pilot message, and that message leaves out the hook |

| **6.4 Understand what remains** | As P1, I am told that events already committed stay in git history, and that kadence cannot erase them | Shipped in wording for `task delete` (0.1.0). **Gap:** not said anywhere about leaving |
## Release slices
### Slice 1 — ICP activation: the first 14 days for the tech lead and a second author
**Goal:** P1 installs, records work and at least one decision, and brings P2 in. By day 14, P2 or P2's agent has written to `.kadence/events` without being asked.
**Measured by:** strategy KR 3.1 (Pilot 0, Sep 25), KR 3.3 (≥ 2 of 3 pilots with a second author by Nov 13) and KR 3.4 (self-serve, 4 of 5).
**What must work.** Almost all of it is already shipped:
| Activity | Stories in the slice |
| 1. Adopt | 1.2 install · 1.3 `init` (+ `--hooks` on Claude Code) · 1.4 columns only · the removal steps visible before install |
| 2. Capture | 2.1 `task add` · 2.2 acceptance criteria |
| 3. Hand off | 3.1 P2 learns it exists and installs · 3.2 `prime` · 3.3 `ready` · 3.4 `task claim` · 3.5 `task show --json` · 3.6 comment / note · 3.8 conflict-free merge |
| 4. Decide | 4.1 `decision add --why --rejected` · 4.4 the next session reads it |
| 5. Review | 5.2 knowing that a second author has appeared |
| 6. Leave | 6.3 a documented removal |
**Gaps on the activation path, in the order they would cost a pilot:**

1. **The second author has no way in (3.1).** The North Star is a second author, and the product does nothing to create one. Today it depends on P1 sending a message we wrote. *Cheapest test:* have the `init` message and the `AGENTS.md` section say, in one line, what a teammate should run. Then watch whether Pilot 0's second person needs anything more.
2. **`decision add` with two `--rejected` crashes on npm (4.1).** It is fixed in the working tree. *Publish before Sep 25*, because the pilot's first handoff is "the lead records one decision".

3. **A teammate without kadence (3.1).** What the `prime` hook does on a machine where kadence is missing has never been checked. It is cheap to check before Pilot 0, and expensive to discover during it.

4. **Agents other than Claude Code (3.2, 4.4).** The ICP explicitly includes multi-vendor teams. For Cursor and Codex, reading `prime` rests on an unobserved instruction in `AGENTS.md`. Pilot notes should record which agents ran `prime` unprompted.
5. **Removal is not written where P1 looks (1.1, 6.3).** The pilot message covers three of the four things `init` can add. It leaves out the hook.
6. **P1 cannot see day 14 in the product (5.2).** The check is a `git log` one-liner. That is acceptable for pilots, but a gap for self-serve.
7. **Self-serve is unobserved (1.6).** KR 3.4 is the only thing that tests whether the README alone is enough.
**Deliberately out of this slice:** sprints, milestones, DoD, every report, exports, the TUI (useful, but it doesn't create a second author), `@kadence/github`, importers.
### Slice 2 — Pilots, gate Fri Nov 13

**Goal:** ≥ 3 concierge pilots, ≥ 2 of them with a second author at day 14, self-serve 4 of 5, and ≥ 3 first-run fixes shipped from what pilots stumbled on (KR 3.2–3.5). The Show HN post on Nov 17 depends on this gate.
- Every slice 1 gap that a pilot actually hit, fixed and published. That is KR 3.5, and it cannot be planned in advance.
- Publish what is Unreleased, so the site, the README and npm say the same thing (`report velocity\|workload\|--list\|--html`, `dist/reference.json`).
- The impact-label recipe (2.4), if a pilot asks.
- `task ac remove` and a less engineering-shaped default DoD (1.4), if pilots put criteria on non-code work.
- `SKILL.md` in marketplaces that list Beads (KR 5.1, Nov 6). This is the agent-side door for 3.2.
- An author count in `stats` (5.2), if the day-14 one-liner proves awkward in pilots.
### Slice 3 — Switchers, conditional: Nov 23 → Jan 15, 2027

**Runs only if** the Oct 19 gate finds ≥ 2 interviewees on a file tracker who describe what switching would cost. The `/from-beads` fake door needs ≥ 2 bookings by Nov 9, or the importer moves to Later.
- 1.5 Backlog.md importer (T67) in 0.6, tested on a real Probe A fixture (KR 6.2, Dec 11)
- 1.5 Beads import (T68), only after the fake door
- 6.2 / 6.4 A clear statement of what a switcher keeps and what they give up
- Outcome: ≥ 1 team we don't control imports and has a second author at day 14 (KR 6.5)
### Slice 4 — 1.0, behind G1–G7 (realistically Q2 2027)
G1 (five public repositories with two authors) is not expected before the Jan 18 kill-clock review ([strategy §3](DOC-35)). 1.0 follows G1.
- **G3 contract:** a 0.x fixture corpus, a deprecation policy, and `schema --json` covering every shipped command (it omits several today)
- **G4 platforms (1.2):** Windows CI; npm, pnpm, yarn and bun smoke tests; `npx`
- **G5 size (1.6):** `doctor`; `board --json` no longer growing with history (855 KB at 1,000 tasks today)
- **G7 human-checked screens:** the TUI checklist run on the release candidate; a length guardrail on the `init` section
- 3.7 identity across machines (SPEC §9); a rebase strategy test
- 6.3 a removal command, if slice 1 shows the written procedure is not enough
### Not on this map, by decision

A web server, a hosted core, accounts, telemetry, two-way sync, time tracking, editor extensions, `llms.txt`, `kadence context`, and an MCP server unless a named user cannot run the CLI ([strategy §8](DOC-35)). A per-model attribution field is a considered "not now", not a "never".
## What changed since the 2026-09-08 map

- **The backbone moved from one developer's sprint to a team's handoff.** The old line (create → pick up → do with an agent → merge → close sprint) ended at velocity. Velocity is now a consequence, and the map ends at leaving.

- **The agent moved from a tool inside one activity to an actor across four.** The old map said a second map, the agent's journey, would be more honest, and deferred that to Probe B. That is still deferred. The agent's stories live inside activities 2–5 here.

- **The old map's three gaps:** "resolve divergences is invisible" stays closed (3.8). "Estimating is the weakest link" no longer matters, because velocity is not on the activation path. "Activity 3 is unmeasured" is still open, and now appears as the three ★ gaps in 3.1, 3.2 and 4.4.
- **The old map had one user; this one has two.** The North Star counts the second, and the most important gap (3.1) is on that person's side.
## What this map still cannot show

- **Whether the job statement is real.** It comes from reasoning and one unsolicited conversation ([tech-lead feedback](../research/tech-lead-feedback-2026-09-10.md)), not from Probe B. If the Oct 19 verdict says 0 stories, activities 3 and 4 shrink and slice 3 becomes the product.

- **Attention versus storage.** The tech lead said drift comes from nobody looking, and a journal only knows what gets written to it. Story 5.2 (`report attention`) is the pull-based answer. Whether a team acts on it is untested.
- **The agent's own journey.** It needs pilot notes on what agents did without being told.
Revisit this map after the Oct 19 verdict and again at the Nov 13 gate.
